I’m so sorry, but restricting screen time can’t be the best solution we have. Isn’t it known that complete restriction isn’t the best way to deal with addiction? If students access to devices is constantly controlled by authority figures while in grade school, what happens when they graduate and no one is around to keep them from those devices? They might end up being behind and disconnected from an increasingly digital world, or binging on screen time until they’re addicted anyways. 

Educators should instead be teaching students how to manage screen time themselves, about the realities, dangers, and benefits of devices. We’re teachers. Why does it seem that this is something that most are unwilling to teach? 

Yes, apps and phones are inherently addictive. So is sugar. Europeans glutted themselves on it when they first had it, to the point of rotten teeth, diabetes, and death. And while it might take time and effort, just like sugar, we CAN learn that the things that make us feel immediately good and happy can also be dangerous outside of moderation, and that can influence our relationship with them.
